description: DamSegment is a Mendeley collection of annotated photographs from an on-site visit to a concrete dam in the United States. Its article describes 3,500 image patches that support crack and spalling classification, detection and segmentation. The current version lists three ZIP archives for those tasks and provides pixel-level masks or boxes in the described subsets. Mendeley states CC BY 4.0. The dataset can test visual damage recognition in dam asset-condition simulations, but image labels do not quantify structural capacity or the time at which a defect formed. One dam, selected image patches and human annotation choices are limitations for transferring a classifier to other structures. A reviewer-assessed use is checking whether a condition-monitoring pipeline detects visible surface damage before a risk model uses those indicators. data-bc-mines-dam-safety-inspection-reports-summary is a related dam inspection resource with different evidence. DamCrack is a separate later deposit by overlapping researchers; its article explicitly names DamSegment as related and reports different image counts. No image archive was downloaded.
